title: Postpartum depression screening
what: You answer a short questionnaire about your mood and how you feel. This helps spot postpartum depression in time.
why: Usually in the first weeks and months after birth. Sometimes during pregnancy too.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes; the doctor discusses the result right away
tell_doctor: If you have anxiety, crying, or irritability
If you have support at home
If you have thoughts of harming yourself or your baby, be sure to say so. You will get help

prepare.title: Honesty
prepare.text: Answer as things really are. There are no right or wrong answers.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Answer about how you felt over the last 1 to 2 weeks.

prepare.title: Support
prepare.text: You can come with someone close to you.

bring: You can bring your baby, if it is allowed
steps: You get a questionnaire on paper or on a phone
The doctor adds up the score
The doctor discusses the result with you
If needed, help or a visit with a specialist is offered
feel: The questions can be personal. This is normal
It can be hard to admit things are difficult. The doctor will understand
after: If the score is low, keep paying attention to how you feel
If it is high, the doctor will offer support, counseling, or treatment
Ask your family for help. Sleep and rest are very important
red_flags: Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby: call emergency services or see a doctor right away
You cannot sleep, eat, or care for your baby for many days in a row

faq.q: Does this mean I am a bad mother?
faq.a: No. Postpartum depression is common, and it can be treated.

faq.q: How are the baby blues different from depression?
faq.a: The baby blues usually pass in 1 to 2 weeks. If you feel bad for longer or more strongly, tell your doctor.

reminders.text: Visit about how you feel after the birth tomorrow. Answer the questions honestly. It will help.
